english: The PREFACE on Festivals and other Days that have none proper, and in Masses for the Dead.
notes: Centred across the full measure above both columns, in two lines. PREFACE is small capitals; the rest alternates italic and roman word by word: italic The, roman PREFACE, italic on, roman Festivals, italic and other Days that have none, roman proper, italic and in, roman Masses, italic for the, roman Dead. The running head over this page and over pp. xxix-xxxii is PREFACES. in small capitals, with the page number in the outer corner.

english: N. B. This mark* refers to the subsequent part of the proper Prefaces.
notes: Centred across the full measure between the heading and the columns; N. B. roman, the rest italic except the closing words proper Prefaces. which are roman. The asterisk is set close up to mark with no space. This note governs the whole apparatus of pp. xxviii-xxxii: no Latin heading is printed anywhere in this section, the headings are English and span both columns.

speaker: priest
english: IT is truly meet and just, right and available to salvation, that we should always, and in all places, give thanks to thee, O holy Lord, Father Almighty, eternal God. * Thro' Christ our Lord: by whom the angels praise thy majesty, the dominations adore it, the powers tremble before it, the heavens, the heavenly virtues, and blessed seraphim, with common jubilee glorify it. Together with whom we beseech thee, that we may be admitted to join our humble voices, saying:
notes: Two-line drop I in IT; the Latin column has the matching two-line drop V in VERE. HOW THE ASTERISK WORKS: the asterisk stands inside this common Preface at the seam, immediately before Thro' Christ our Lord (Latin * Per Christum Dominum nostrum), i.e. between eternal God. and Thro'. Every proper Preface on pp. xxviii-xxxii opens with an asterisk and is printed as the clause alone; the reader inserts it at this point, then resumes here at the second asterisk. A proper Preface that ends * Thro' &c. or * Per Christum, &c. or * By whom, &c. or * And, &c. resumes the common text at exactly this asterisk; one that ends with a dagger instead resumes at the conclusion of the Christmas Preface (see praefatio-de-nativitate). Scan damage: in seraphim the terminal m has broken strokes and reads seraphiin at 1600 dpi; read against the facing Latin seraphim and against the same word printed sound in the English column of p. xxix. The book uses French spacing, a thin space before colon and semicolon (agere : dicentes :); that spacing is not reproduced here.

speaker: priest
english: Holy, holy, holy, Lord God of Sabaoth. Heaven and earth are full of thy glory. Hosanna in the highest. Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord, Hosanna in the highest.
notes: Set as a separate indented paragraph after a blank line in both columns; the book prints no speaker attribution and no rubric over it. The Sanctus is printed ONCE only, here; it is never reprinted after any proper Preface, which are cued Holy, &c. in English and Sanctus, &c. in Latin.

english: On TRINITY-SUNDAY, and every other Sunday in the Year that has no proper Preface.
notes: Centred across the full measure in two lines. TRINITY-SUNDAY in small capitals; On italic, and every other italic, Sunday roman, in the Year that has italic, no proper italic, Preface. roman.

speaker: priest
english: * Who together with thy only begotten Son and the Holy Ghost, art one God, and one Lord not in a singularity of one Person, but in a Trinity of one substance. For what we believe of thy glory, as thou hast revealed, the same we believe of thy Son, and of the Holy Ghost, without any difference or distinction. So that in the confession of the true and eternal Deity, we adore a distinction in the Persons, an unity in the essence, and an equality in the Majesty. Whom the angels and archangels, the cherubim also and seraphim praise: and cease not daily to cry out with one voice saying, Holy, &c.
notes: The clause only, not a whole Preface: it opens with the asterisk and is inserted at the asterisk of praefatio-communis. Runs over the page break, breaking at art / one God between p. xxviii and p. xxix. No comma after one Lord, as printed. Scan damage at the right margin of p. xxix, all controlled at 1600 dpi against the facing Latin: believe of loses the f (prints as believe o, Latin hoc de Filio tuo); reveal- keeps only a blot where the hyphen was (revealed, Latin revelante); the end-of-line hyphen of Dei-ty is eaten entirely, the page printing Dei at the end of one line and ty, at the start of the next (Latin Deitatis); begotten at the foot of p. xxviii reads begotteu, the n having lost its right shoulder. The Latin column here prints Quam laudant angeli where the Roman text has Quem, and sets no full stop after æqualitas.

english: From CHRISTMAS-DAY till the Epiphany; on Corpus Christi; and on our Lord's Transfiguration.
notes: Centred across the full measure in two lines. CHRISTMAS-DAY in small capitals; From, till the, on, and on in italic, the rest roman. The book sets a thin space before the first semicolon (Epiphany ; on); not reproduced.

english: N. B. Prefaces thus marked † are concluded in the same manner as this.
notes: Centred across the full measure between the heading and the columns, in two lines; N. B. Prefaces roman, the rest italic. The mark is an obelus (dagger) used as a reference mark, printed in the English column itself and so kept here; it is not a cross of blessing. Its force: a proper Preface whose text ends at a dagger takes the conclusion of THIS Christmas Preface from its dagger onward, i.e. And therefore with the angels and archangels ... saying, Holy, &c., instead of rejoining the common Preface at the asterisk.

speaker: priest
english: * Since by the mystery of the Word made flesh, a new ray of thy glory has appeared to the eyes of our souls: that while we behold God visibly, we may be carried by him to the love of things invisible. † And therefore with the angels and archangels, with the thrones and dominations; and with all the heavenly host, we sing an everlasting hymn to thy glory, saying, Holy, &c.
notes: The clause plus a conclusion: asterisk at the head, dagger before And therefore. Not a whole Preface; the opening Vere dignum is not reprinted. Runs over the page break, breaking at with the / thrones between p. xxix and p. xxx. Scan damage: the end-of-line hyphen of everlast-ing is eaten entirely at the right margin of p. xxx, the page printing everlast at the end of one line and ing at the start of the next; read at 1600 dpi against the facing Latin hymnum gloriæ tuæ canimus. The hyphen of ap-peared is present but clipped. The Latin column of p. xxix has two broken sorts before invisibilium amorem where the Roman text reads in invisibilium amorem.

english: On the Epiphany and during its Octave.
notes: Centred across the full measure on one line. No small capitals in this heading, unlike its neighbours: On the italic, Epiphany roman, and during its italic, Octave. roman.

speaker: priest
latin_incipit: Quia cum unigenitus tuus in substantia
english: * Because when thy only begotten Son appeared in the substance of our mortal flesh, he repaired us by the new light of his immortality. † And therefore, &c.
notes: The clause only; asterisk at the head, and the dagger cue at the end refers the reader to the conclusion of the Christmas Preface. The final line † And therefore, &c. is set flush left as a short line of its own, matching the Latin † Et ideo, &c.

english: In LENT till Passion-Sunday.
notes: Centred across the full measure on one line. LENT in small capitals; In and till in italic, Passion-Sunday. roman.

speaker: priest
english: * Who by this bodily fast extinguishest our vices, elevatest our understanding, bestowest on us virtue and its reward. * Thro' &c.
notes: The clause only. It closes with an asterisk, not a dagger, so it rejoins the common Preface: the English cue is * Thro' &c. with NO comma after Thro' (verified at 1600 dpi), where the parallel cue on the next Preface has one; the Latin cue is * Per Christum, &c.

english: On PASSION and PALM SUNDAYS, Maundy-Thursday, and Feasts of the Holy Cross.
notes: Centred across the full measure in two lines. PASSION and PALM SUNDAYS in small capitals; On, and, and, of the in italic, the rest roman.

speaker: priest
latin_incipit: Qui salutem humam generis in ligno
english: * Who hast appointed that the salvation of mankind should be wrought on the wood of the cross: that from whence death came, thence life might arise, and that he who overcame by the tree, might also by the tree be overcome. * Thro', &c.
notes: The clause only; closes with an asterisk and so rejoins the common Preface, cue * Thro', &c. (with comma). Scan damage: man-kind is broken at the right margin but the hyphen survives. The Latin column prints humam generis for humani generis, a misprint of the book, verified at 1600 dpi; and closes Christum. &c. with a full stop where a comma is wanted. The latin_incipit above reproduces the misprint as printed.

english: From HOLY SATURDAY till the Ascension.
notes: Centred across the full measure on one line. HOLY SATURDAY in small capitals; From and till the in italic, Ascension. roman.

speaker: priest
english: IT is truly meet and just, right and available to salvation, to praise thee, O Lord, at all times, but chiefly on this [night or day, or, at this time] when Christ our Passover was sacrificed for us. For he is the true Lamb who hath taken away the sins of the world. Who by dying has destroyed our death, and by rising again has restored us to life. † And
notes: NOT a clause: this Preface is printed WHOLE, from Vere dignum, with the same two-line drop I and drop V as the common Preface, because its body differs from the common one. Runs over the page break, breaking at avail- / able between p. xxx and p. xxxi. DEFECT: the English column stops dead at † And at the foot of its last line and the Ascension heading follows immediately; therefore, &c. is simply not set, though the facing Latin closes † Et ideo, &c. Verified at 1600 dpi that nothing follows And and that no line has been lost to the gutter or the margin. Scan damage: after our death the comma has lost its tail and survives only as a dot below the line; read as a comma against the Latin destruxit, et vitam. The square brackets round night or day, or, at this time are the book's own, matching the Latin brackets round in hoc potissimum nocte vel die, vel; the opening Latin bracket has printed as a broken sort.

english: From ASCENSION-DAY till Whitsun-Eve.
notes: Centred across the full measure on one line. ASCENSION-DAY in small capitals; From and till in italic, Whitsun-Eve. roman.

speaker: priest
latin_incipit: Per Christum Dominum nostrum. Qui post
english: * Through Christ our Lord. Who after his resurrection appeared openly to all his disciples, and in their presence ascended into heaven, to make us partakers of his divine nature. † And therefore, &c.
notes: The clause only. Note that here and in the Whitsuntide Preface the book spells the word out, Through Christ our Lord, where the common Preface and the Lent and Passion cues have Thro'. Ends at a dagger and so takes the Christmas conclusion.

english: From WHITSUN-EVE till Trinity-Sunday; and in Votive Masses of the Holy Ghost.
notes: Centred across the full measure in two lines. WHITSUN-EVE in small capitals; From, till, and in, of the in italic, the rest roman. In the word in of and in the i has lost its dot.

speaker: priest
latin_incipit: Per Christum Dominum nostrum. Qui ascendens
english: * Through Christ our Lord. Who ascending above all the heavens, and sitting at thy right hand, didst send down the promised holy Spirit [this day] upon the children of adoption. Wherefore the whole world displays its excess of joy. The heavenly virtues also and all the angelic powers, sing in concert an everlasting hymn to thy glory, saying, Holy, &c.
notes: The clause with its own conclusion (no dagger; it runs on to saying, Holy, &c.). Runs over the page break, breaking at angelic pow- / ers between p. xxxi and p. xxxii. Square brackets round this day are the book's own, matching the Latin [hodierna die]. Scan damage at the right margin of p. xxxi, controlled at 1600 dpi against the facing Latin: the end-of-line hyphen of chil-dren is eaten entirely, the page printing chil at the end of one line and dren at the start of the next (Latin in filios adoptionis); in also the final o is clipped to a crescent (Latin Sed et supernæ virtutes). The book prints holy Spirit with a lower-case h.

english: On FESTIVALS of the B. V. MARY (the Purification excepted.)
notes: Centred across the full measure in two lines. FESTIVALS and MARY in small capitals, B. V. in full capitals; On and of the in italic, and the parenthesis the Purification excepted. in italic. The full stop stands INSIDE the closing parenthesis, as printed.

speaker: priest
latin_incipit: Et te in N. Beatæ Mariæ
english: * That we should praise, bless, and glorify thee on the N. ‡ of the blessed Mary, ever a Virgin. Who by the overshadowing of the Holy Ghost conceived thy only begotten Son: and the glory of her virginity still remaining, brought forth the eternal light of the world, Jesus Christ our Lord. * By whom, &c.
notes: The clause only; closes with an asterisk and rejoins the common Preface, cue * By whom, &c. (Latin * Per quem, &c.). The mark after N. is a double dagger, printed in both columns and keyed to the footnote at the foot of the page; verified at 1600 dpi. Scan damage at the right margin: in and the the final e is clipped, in still the final l is thinned, and the hyphen of Vir-gin is raised and partly clipped; all read against the facing Latin Beatæ Mariæ semper Virginis / Virginitatis gloria permanente. The book sets a thin space before the colon in Son : and; not reproduced.

english: On the FESTIVALS of the APOSTLES.
notes: Centred across the full measure on one line. FESTIVALS and APOSTLES in small capitals; On the and of the in italic.

speaker: priest
english: IT is truly meet and just, right and available to salvation, humbly to beseech thee that thou O Lord, our eternal Shepherd wouldst not forsake thy flock, but keep it under thy continual protection by thy blessed apostles. That it may be governed by those whom thou hast appointed its vicars and pastors. * And, &c.
notes: NOT a clause: printed WHOLE from Vere dignum with the two-line drop I and drop V, like the Easter Preface, since its body replaces the common one; it nevertheless closes with an asterisk cue * And, &c. (Latin * Et ideo, &c.). No comma after thou, and none after Shepherd, as printed. A small raised mark stands after right in the second line; it matches no whole comma or apostrophe, the parallel opening on p. xxviii prints just, right and available with nothing after right, and it is read here as a broken sort or ink speck and not transcribed. This is the last block printed on p. xxxii apart from the footnote below; the next page opens THE CANON OF THE MASS.

english: ‡ Here the Name of her several Festivals, as they occur in the course of the Year, should be expressed.
notes: Footnote set in italic across the full measure at the foot of the page, below both columns and below the Apostles Preface, separated by a blank line. It is keyed to the double dagger in the Preface of the Blessed Virgin. Its own leading mark is the double dagger.
